commentary_segments.text: Two such inverter amplifiers are used for differential operation as shown in this slide. Both a bipolar and a CMOS version are shown. The tuning is carried out by current I. In the bipolar one (on the left) the common-mode current through the diodes in the middle is four times larger than any other inverter branch. It is a differential circuit, as each change of current in one inverter causes the opposite current in the other inverter. The CMOS realization (on the right), is very similar. CMFB is used to avoid common-mode offset caused by the mismatch between the top and bottom current sources I. In both realizations, the equivalent input noise is quite low as only the four input transistors contribute to it.
